title: CtlOpRequest
description:
The body of EVERY mutating call (`POST /v1/tenants/{name}/ops/{verb}`, `POST /v1/gateway/apply`, `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/{resume|continue|cancel}`, `PUT /v1/settings`) — `POST /v1/tenants` uses the same envelope with typed args (`create_request.json`).

`dry_run: true` → 200 `plan.json`, nothing is locked or written. `dry_run: false` → 202 `job.json`, or one of the 409/428 refusals. `idempotency_key` is chosen by the client and PERSISTED with `(principal, op, tenant, normalized args, plan digest)`: a retry with the same key and the same request returns the ORIGINAL job (202, same `id`); the same key with a different request is 409 `duplicate`. `confirm` must equal the plan's `confirm_value` when the plan said `requires_confirm` (428 `confirm_required` otherwise). `ctl_api_key` is how a BROWSER authorizes a mutation: a session authenticates reads only, so the UI prompts for the key per request and sends it here, never storing it; when the request already carries `X-API-Key`, `ctl_api_key` may be omitted and, if present, must be the same key (else 400 `both_credentials`). `args` is the verb's typed argument object (documented per verb in `openapi.yaml`'s `x-ctl-op-args`); `{}` for verbs without arguments.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated, unique per intended mutation — a UUID or ULID is the expected shape.

force_with_doctor_diff.description: Quote the `doctor.hash` of a YELLOW plan to proceed past its warnings — the CLI's `--force-with-doctor-diff HASH`. Never bypasses a red status, authorization, containment, ownership or fencing.
